title: Mic gain, ALC and the speech processor
idea: Mic gain sets how hard your voice drives the transmitter. ALC holds back peaks so the amplifier isn't overdriven; too much drive and the peaks flat-top. A speech processor raises average power so you sound louder.

rows: Distortion from excessive drive or speech levels

compare.how: How hard your voice drives the transmitter. Sets the ALC.
Holds peaks back to prevent excessive drive.
Raises average power, not peak power.

traps.why: ALC is set with the transmit audio or microphone gain.
Peaks stay the same; average power goes up.
It makes you sound louder; overdone, it adds distortion.

traps.wrong: The transmitter’s automatic level control (ALC) is properly adjusted
traps.why: Flat-topping is distortion from too much drive or speech level.

traps.wrong: When using digital modes, too much ALC activity can cause the transmitter to overheat
traps.why: The reason is that ALC action distorts the data signal.
